title: Reopen deterministic engine completeness under the clause-capability contract
description:
Provider-neutral deterministic engine/tool capability work, reopened under the clause-capability contract established by the 2026-07-24 SRD audit repair program (eshyra-o9bd.19).

SEPARATION OF CONCERNS — the reason this epic exists outside eshyra-o9bd.19:
  * The PACK question (eshyra-o9bd.19) is whether the data completely and
    accurately expresses the rules.
  * The ENGINE question (this epic) is whether Eshyra can execute the rules the
    pack expresses.
These interact but must never again become indistinguishable. An engine-pending
clause is NOT automatically a pack defect. Conversely, no engine gap may remain
invisible: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 (bootstrap ledger) and eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12
(authoritative ledger) own the inventory and the ownership gate that guarantee
every requirement here has a real owner.

Capabilities implemented here are PROVIDER-NEUTRAL engine primitives. They are
not SRD-specific runtime branches, and must not be implemented as such: the SRD
5.1 pack is the first consumer that exercises them, not their definition.

Children are the engine:F1..engine:F10 capability families. Exact membership is
owned by the ledger beads; do not hand-copy counts into acceptance criteria.

*** engine:F* IS A QUALIFIED PREFIX — see eshyra-o9bd.19.5 for the full
taxonomy-collision warning. engine:F1..F10 (pack executionReadiness engineHooks)
are NOT the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t's F1-F10, and NOT the fable:F1..F8 audit
findings.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every engine:F* family is implemented as a provider-neutral capability with executable conformance scenarios driven from pack clause data.
- Unsupported clauses fail CLOSED at runtime; no silent degradation.
- Every capability required by the authoritative ledger (eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12) is green or carries an approved explicit house-rule/design dependency.
- No capability is closed by asserting the pack is data-complete.
- The release/re-freeze gate can depend on this epic and eshyra-o9bd.19 jointly for end-to-end playability.
notes:
Supersedes the scope ambition of the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t, which used a DIFFERENT F1-F10 taxonomy. Do not treat eshyra-2n1t's closure as evidence of engine completeness; eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 owns the four-way reconciliation of that contradiction.
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.
*** DECOMPOSITION IS MACHINE-GATED (2026-07-25) ***
bd forbids epic->task dependencies, so this epic cannot itself depend on the
bootstrap ledger. Instead:

  eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 bootstrap ledger
    -> "Authorize Engine F1-F10 decomposition ..." (shared, under this epic)
    -> ten per-family "Decompose Engine F<n> ..." tasks
    -> implementation children (created only by those decomposition tasks)
    -> ten per-family "Certify Engine F<n> ..." tasks
    -> "Certify the deterministic reference engine for SRD re-freeze"
    -> eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 -> ... -> eshyra-o9bd.14 formal re-freeze

The ten Engine F epics still appear in bd ready. That is a bd display
limitation, not permission to start: every executable task beneath them is
blocked by the authorization gate. Do not dispatch implementation agents to an
Engine F epic; the first legitimate work in each is its decomposition task.

*** IDS ARE HISTORICAL, NOT PATHS (2026-07-25) ***
The ten family epics keep their eshyra-o9bd.19.5.* IDs on purpose. Bead IDs are
durable historical identifiers; recreating them for cosmetically matching
eshyra-olc5.* IDs would invalidate references already placed in bead
descriptions and the finding registry, create confusing duplicates, and
complicate audit archaeology. Judge parentage by the tree, and query the family
set by the "engine-capability" label rather than by ID prefix.
*** ADR 0020 NARROWING (2026-07-31) — SUPERSEDES THE ZERO-ENGINE-PENDING BAR ***
Authority: ADR 0020, and the integrated transition design
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md
sections 5.4, 5.5, 5.9 — the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8
(PR #485, reviewed head afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). Recorded here as accepted authority;
NOT implemented in code by this bead update.

1. engine:F1..engine:F10 IS THE GENERATED MAGIC-ITEM CAPABILITY BACKLOG, not a
   corpus-wide engine inventory. Verified extent: 240 records carrying
   executionReadiness — all of kind magic-item — 1,016 clauses, of which 794 are
   engine-pending, 218 green, 3 adjudicated-by-design, 1 design-blocked; 795
   clauses carry non-empty engineHooks. No other record kind carries
   executionReadiness. The 794 and 795 counts are two different predicates over
   the same data: magic-item:candle-of-invocation/c1-burn-time is GREEN while
   still declaring an F5 hook, so "green" is not interchangeable with
   "hook-free", and neither count may be reported as a capability inventory.
   The ten family epics are REASSESSED against that bounded scope, not deleted:
   221 of 240 items still carry at least one engine-pending or design-blocked
   clause, and those obligations remain real.

2. "AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES" IS NO
   LONGER THE RE-FREEZE BAR. It requires a global negative the corpus cannot
   support: RulesRecord.data is typed unknown (rules/types.ts:135), kind
   validators accept unregistered data fields, and key closure over mechanics
   exists for magic-item only. The replacement is the nine-condition truthfulness
   bar in section 5.9 of the transition design, recorded on eshyra-o9bd.14 and
   eshyra-2zyy. Nothing in the new bar requires global deterministic closure,
   universal discovery completeness, zero engine-pending clauses, or a
   corpus-wide negative claim of any kind. The nine-point GREEN definition above
   stands as a per-clause quality definition for clauses that ARE positively
   selected for deterministic execution; it is no longer a corpus-wide gate.

3. CAPABILITY WORK IS A SET OF POSITIVE, BOUNDED COMMITMENTS (ADR 0020 section
   3). A capability declares what operation it performs, its required inputs, its
   exclusions, its revision or identity, and what interpretation remains with the
   DM — and fails closed on unrecognized input.

4. eshyra-olc5.6 (transition W13) OWNS CAPABILITY-CONTRACT NORMALIZATION: putting
   every capability in force into that five-field shape and proving fail-closed
   behavior. It depends on eshyra-uiax (the unrecognized-scope fail-open on the
   pilot contract assertMagicItemOperationReady) and on the
   ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE split owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.14 (transition W14).
   It creates no corpus-wide capability inventory and does not widen
   engine:F1..F10 beyond the generated magic-item backlog.

5. ABSENCE OF A CAPABILITY BINDING PROVES ONLY THAT NO CAPABILITY WAS POSITIVELY
   SELECTED. It is a statement about Eshyra, not about the rules. It never means
   the record has no mechanics, the rule is irrelevant or unsupported, the rule
   can be ignored, or the pack is mechanically complete. "Unbound",
   "unclassified", and "not recognized" are not safety properties; any gate,
   report, or predicate that reads an unbound or unrecognized item as satisfied
   is a defect, not a green. Symmetrically, a deterministic operation does not
   imply a complete record: magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3 carries one green,
   positively owned clause (c1-use) and one engine-pending clause
   (c2-static-ammunition-rarity-attack-damage, F8) simultaneously.
